supersession_note: v1.0 is NOT edited and NOT retired. It is committed evidence bound into the WP-C/WP-D submission. Directions D-S1 through D-S6 and standing rule SR-HOST-1 carry forward unchanged EXCEPT where amended below. This v1.1 adds the control-boundary ruling that host qualification and validation credential release are separate acts.

occasion.trigger: The WP-D placeholder trust policy on mr002-validation-reader names a future run-host role. As encoded, provisioning and naming that host role would BE the credential release — collapsing host qualification and P12 into a single edit.
occasion.owner_ruling: Those two controls do not need to be the same act, and must not be. Qualification identifies the future grantee; P12 activates the grant.

directions_added.subject: Separation of host qualification from validation credential release
directions_added.direction: Host qualification MUST NOT satisfy or partially satisfy P12. Creating and qualifying the Phase 3C host is a runtime-identity act; releasing validation-partition credentials is an authorization act. They are sequenced, not merged.
required_sequence: 1. Provision the Phase 3C host ROLE and instance profile with NO validation-partition access and NO ability to assume mr002-validation-reader. Grant only what is needed to exist and be qualified: container/ECR pull for the bound evaluator image, plus logging/SSM if already part of the operational model.

2. Provision the actual host using that role and QUALIFY it: instance/role identity, OS + container runtime, architecture and CPU characteristics, evaluator-image resolution path, and every other host requirement already bound by the Phase 3A package.

3. Capture P10 prospectively on that host THROUGH WP-B ONLY. The Requirement-7 resolver pulls the immutable evaluator image from ECR; that requires no validation-data credential. P10 is therefore satisfiable while validation_authorization = false at _rev 0.
4. Freeze P10 under SR-HOST-1 and re-evaluate P6–P11 as a complete set — the actual runtime identity now exists WITHOUT validation access having been opened.
5. Authorize and run WP-F separately, proving C1–C10 + C-R7 against the qualified host and the then-current tree, WHILE the validation reader is still unassumable.

6. ONLY after WP-F PASS and D3 adjudication does P12 edit the reader-role trust policy to name the already-qualified host role. That edit IS the explicit, durable credential-release event. The CAS false → true follows, and validation access is permitted only afterward.
directions_added.principle: Qualification identifies the future grantee; P12 activates the grant.

directions_added.subject: What P12 binds to
directions_added.direction: P12 MUST bind to the qualified instance-profile / IAM ROLE identity plus the frozen host and runtime evidence. It MUST NOT bind to an EC2 instance ID.
directions_added.why: An instance is ephemeral and replaceable; the role is the security principal. Binding authorization to an instance identifier would make the authorization model depend on a disposable identifier, and would force a re-authorization for any instance replacement even when the security principal and runtime identity are unchanged.
directions_added.division_of_labour: The ROLE carries the authorization. SR-HOST-1 carries the numeric-runtime concern: replacing the actual execution host invalidates P10 and forces requalification, without the authorization model touching an EC2 identifier at all.

standing_rules.rule: Host replacement before validation INVALIDATES P10 and requires a fresh P10 capture and a re-run of grant-readiness verification.
standing_rules.amendment: Replacement of the actual execution host additionally requires REQUALIFICATION per D-S7 step 2. The rule is scoped to the numeric runtime and does not, by itself, revoke or re-open the P12 authorization, which is bound to the role identity per D-S8.
standing_rules.failure_mode_prevented: A NumericRuntimeIdentityManifest generated on Host A while execution silently moves to Host B.

standing_rules.rule: The mr002-validation-reader trust policy is the credential-release control. It may be edited ONLY as the P12 authorization event, after WP-F PASS and D3 adjudication. No other work package may edit it for any reason.
standing_rules.current_state: Trust policy names arn:aws:iam::219024422756:role/mr002-phase3c-run-host-NOT-YET-PROVISIONED. Verified 2026-08-11: that role does NOT exist, and no role matching 'phase3c' exists in the account. The grant is inert.
standing_rules.expected_transition: The P12 edit WILL change this hash. That change is the authorized transition, not tampering. A verifier re-checking AFTER P12 must expect a mismatch against the P11 snapshot; WP-F runs BEFORE P12 and must match it exactly.

trap_to_avoid.severity: HIGH — would silently consume P12 during qualification
trap_to_avoid.detail: The placeholder is a LITERAL STRING in a StringEquals condition on aws:PrincipalArn. If the Phase 3C host role were provisioned with the literal name 'mr002-phase3c-run-host-NOT-YET-PROVISIONED', the condition would match and the reader role would become assumable the moment the host role existed — releasing validation credentials during qualification, exactly what D-S7 forbids, and with no edit to any policy to mark the event.
trap_to_avoid.requirement: The real host role MUST be given a DIFFERENT name (e.g. 'mr002-phase3c-run-host'). Confirm before creation that the chosen name is not the placeholder string.
trap_to_avoid.detection: Any successful sts:AssumeRole against mr002-validation-reader before the recorded P12 event is an integrity failure and is visible as a CloudTrail management event.

next_owner_decision.narrow_framing: Authorize provisioning of a QUALIFICATION-ONLY Phase 3C host, with no validation-reader trust relationship and no validation/OOS access.
next_owner_decision.why_this_framing: It obtains the only remaining producible prerequisite (P10) without risk of consuming P12 while doing so.
